findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Senate Second Reading, Roll Call #693 (passed 28-13)
findings.note: Senator Galey is listed among the ayes on Senate second reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The bill's digest (https://webservices.ncleg.gov/BillDigests/2025/H958, fetched) describes changes touching the subject: military-overseas ballots must come with photo ID or an affidavit, the deadline to provide ID after a provisional ballot rises from the third to the fifth business day, a voter registration is processed only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship, and a full social security number is required to register. The digest covers several bill editions, so not every item is necessarily in the version voted on.

findings.note: Senate second-reading vote on HB 958, Election Law Changes (roll call 2026-07-28, 6:13 PM): Galey voted Aye, 28 to 13. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds G.S. 163-83, under which a county board processes a registration application only if it affirmatively says the applicant is a U.S. citizen. A blank answer gets a notice, and a statement under penalty of perjury is required within 30 days. It also bars driver-license-office staff from proceeding with a registration unless the applicant says they are a citizen, and it requires a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens in a federal database. The bill page shows the bill was vetoed 2026-08-17. She also voted Aye on Amendments 1 and 5 and Aye on motions to table Amendments 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register
voter-roll checks and removal of non-citizens
election integrity laws in general

findings.note: Listed as a co-sponsor (not primary) of SB 630, Constitutional Amendment/Citizens-Only Voting. As filed 2023-04-05 (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/PDF/S630v0.pdf), it would put a question on the ballot to provide that only a citizen of the United States who is 18 and otherwise qualified may vote.
